'''Christopher John Fardo Williams''' (31 December 1930 – 25 March 1997)<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last1=Swinburne |first1=Richard |date=29 March 1997 |title=Obituary: Professor C. J. F. Williams |work=[[The Independent]] |location=London |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-professor-c-j-f-williams-1275651.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005104457/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-professor-c-j-f-williams-1275651.html |archive-date=5 October 2013 |accessdate=22 September 2020}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Citation |last=Bary |first=Philip de |editor-first1=A.C |editor-first2=Naomi |editor-first3=Andrew |editor-last1=Grayling |editor-last2=Goulder |editor-last3=Pyle |title=Williams, Christopher John Fardo |date=2006 |url=https://philarchive.org/rec/FERCEO |encyclopedia=The Continuum Encyclopedia of British Philosophy |postscript= |publisher=Continuum |language=en |doi=10.1093/acref/9780199754694.001.0001 |isbn=978-0-19-975469-4 |access-date=2022-06-06|hdl=11693/51028 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> was a British philosopher. His areas of interest were [[philosophical logic]], on which topic he did most of his original work, and [[ancient philosophy]], as an editor and translator.

==Life==
Christopher Williams was born in Walsall<ref name=":0" /> and was educated at [[Shrewsbury School]] and [[Balliol College]], [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] where he took a First in Greats and became a convert to Roman Catholicism, a faith to which he was openly devoted for the rest of his life. Planning to enter the [[Benedictine Order]], he became a novice at [[Downside Abbey]], but shortly thereafter was affected by polio which left him paralysed from the waist down.<ref name=":1" />

Instead he became an academic philosopher, lecturing at the [[University of Hull]] before moving to Bristol, where he taught in the philosophy department as lecturer, Reader and Professor until his retirement in 1996.<ref name=":0" /> Despite his disability, Williams commuted between Bristol and his home in [[Midsomer Norton]] and attended many philosophical conferences around the world. He also edited the philosophy journal, ''[[Analysis (journal)|Analysis]]''.

==Thought==
Believing that such fundamental concepts as existence, truth and identity had been widely misunderstood by the philosophical tradition, and obfuscated especially by [[metaphysics]], Williams attempted to show that they could be elucidated by a close analysis of the way those and related terms are actually used. Williams was not, however, an [[ordinary language]] philosopher; rather, he produced painstaking analyses of the concepts couched in the terms of symbolic logic. In this approach, founded in the logical work of [[Gottlob Frege]], he was most immediately influenced by [[Arthur Prior]] and by his friend and fellow [[Roman Catholic]] philosopher [[Peter Geach]].

He summarized his views in a trilogy of books, ''What is Truth?'' (1976), ''What is Existence?'' (1981) and ''What is Identity?'' (1989), and produced a more accessible overview, with less emphasis on symbolic logic, in a single volume, ''Being, Truth and Identity'' (1992).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Reed |first=Robert C. |date=April 1995 |title=Review of C. J. F. Williams, Being, Identity, and Truth |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/modern-logic/volume-5/issue-2/Review-of-C-J-F-Williams-Being-Identity-and-Truth/rml/1204835490.full |journal=Modern Logic |volume=5 |issue=2 |pages=201–211 |issn=1047-5982 |postscript=. ([[Open Access]] download)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Denyer |first=Nicholas |date=1994 |title=Review of Being, Identity and Truth. |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2220155 |journal=[[The Philosophical Quarterly]] |volume=44 |issue=174 |pages=117–120 |doi=10.2307/2220155 |jstor=2220155 |issn=0031-8094 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Works==
'''Books (authored)'''
*''[[iarchive:whatistruth0000will|What is Truth?]]'' (1976)
*''What is Existence?'' (1981)
*''[[iarchive:whatisidentity0000will|What is Identity?]]'' (1989)
*''Being, Truth and Identity'' (1992).
'''Select papers and book chapters'''

* [[iarchive:petergeachphilos0000unse/page/195/mode/1up|"On Sameness and Selfhood"]], in Harry A. Lewis (ed.), ''[[iarchive:petergeachphilos0000unse|Peter Geach: Philosophical Encounters]]'' (1991).
'''Other works'''

* (Translation. with notes), [[Aristotle]], ''[[iarchive:aristotlesdegene0000aris|De generatione et corruptione]]'' (1982).
* (Edited. with translation and notes), [[Paul of Venice]], ''Logica Magna'' ''[pt 1, fasc. 8]'', ''Tractatus de necessitate et contingentia futurorum'' (1991)
* (Translation) [[John Philoponus]], ''On Aristotle's "On Coming-to-Be and Perishing" 1.1-5,'' and ''On Aristotle's "On Coming-to-Be and Perishing" 1.6-2.4'' (1999)
